clue.text: Collect a ship symbol? Almost

parts.note: SS is the standard abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: an emblem is a symbol

explanation.surface: Someone asked to gather a ship's insignia answers that they nearly have it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from EMBLEM to leave EMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect people or things is to gather them together.

clue.text: He gives a paper cover to a horizontal member

definitions.meaning: a part-time local reporter who covers stories for a newspaper
a long horizontal beam in a building or bridge frame

explanation.surface: Someone supplies a newspaper wrapping to a beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' here is the journalist's sense: to report on an event.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a freelance correspondent paid by the piece and a lengthwise structural timber carry this name.

clue.text: Pip's were great

parts.note: Pip is the hero of the Dickens novel whose title calls his hopes of fortune great

explanation.surface: A boy named Pip had big hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip is the narrator of Dickens's novel Great Expectations, so his hopes were 'great' in the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes of future fortune are what the novel's title names, and the clue completes its two-word title.

clue.text: Europeans disguised as Bengalis

indicators.note: disguised means the letters of the next word appear in a different form

explanation.surface: People from Europe pretend to be from Bengal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised as' rearranges BENGALIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Belgium are people from a European country.

clue.text: Foreign letter records the Italian side

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
il is Italian for the
the on side is one half of the cricket field

explanation.surface: A letter from abroad mentions the records and the Italian team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, so foreign to English.

clue.text: Crush that is in the club

parts.note: to crush food is to mash it
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A crush happens inside the nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: An old golf iron with a lofted face, roughly the modern five iron.

clue.text: Part of London said to figure in "The Boy Friend"

indicators.note: said means the word is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Bow is a district of East London

explanation.surface: A London district is supposedly mentioned in the musical The Boy Friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boy Friend is a musical, but here it simply means a sweetheart; Bow is an East London district.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a male sweetheart or admirer.

clue.text: Subjected to strain and upset, losing the girl

indicators.note: losing means a part of the word is lost from it

parts.note: upset means distressed
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: Someone under pressure and upset after losing their girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes DI from the front of DISTRESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put under strain carries a load of pressure or tension.

clue.text: Deep-sounding scheme against a chap

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: A gloomy plot is set against a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent sounds are loud, resonant and mournful, so deep in tone.

clue.text: This bit of water may be acid

definitions.text: This bit of water may be acid

parts.words: This bit of water may be acid
parts.note: a tiny quantity of liquid falling from a tap, and a sour boiled sweet named acid

explanation.surface: A small amount of liquid might be acidic.
explanation.walkthrough: An acid drop is a sharp-tasting boiled sweet popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rounded quantity of liquid, and also a kind of sweet, as in an acid one.

clue.text: Learner feeling thus perhaps whilst playing this

definitions.text: Learner feeling thus perhaps whilst playing this

indicators.note: playing means the letters of the words perform in a new arrangement

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A beginner might feel this way when playing the instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges L, FEELING and THUS; the whole clue also describes a novice playing the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The recorder used to be called by this name, an end-blown woodwind pipe that beginners often learn.

clue.text: Crudely trapped one lone butterfly

indicators.note: crudely means the letters are roughly put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single solitary butterfly has been roughly caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crudely' rearranges TRAPPED, I and LONE; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterflies and moths belong to the insect order Lepidoptera, so one is a member of that order.

clue.text: She features in articles about a Philistine city

indicators.note: about means the article letters go round the city

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, taken twice
Gath was one of the five Philistine cities in the Bible, home of Goliath

explanation.surface: A woman appears in pieces written about an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps A and A round GATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as in the crime writer Christie.

clue.text: Go beyond the bridge

definitions.meaning: a road crossing above another road

explanation.surface: Travel past the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass something is to exceed it, and a flyover is a road raised over another road.

clue.text: "Come you back, you ______ soldier" (Kipling)

parts.note: a line from Kipling's poem Mandalay with the missing nationality to be filled in

explanation.surface: A quotation from Kipling with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Kipling's Mandalay; the missing word describes the soldier's nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The soldier addressed in the poem is from the United Kingdom, filling the gap.

clue.text: Spread litter round the cattle range

indicators.note: round means the bedding goes around the ranch

parts.note: litter is straw bedding for animals, a bed
a ranch is a cattle range

explanation.surface: Someone scatters straw around the cattle farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Litter is animal bedding here, not rubbish or a brood of young.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree that has branched has spread out into limbs.

clue.text: Benevolent Russian family

parts.note: kind means benevolent
Red was a common label for a Soviet Russian

explanation.surface: A generous family from Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: Red stands for Russian through Soviet-era usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred are relatives, one's kin.

clue.text: Brood in the island on the extremes of temperature

parts.note: Cuba is the Caribbean island

indicators.note: extremes of means the first and last letters of temperature are taken

explanation.surface: Someone sulks on a Caribbean island in very hot or cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes T and E, the first and last letters of temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood eggs is to sit on them to hatch them.

clue.text: Regularity needs a level head

parts.note: even means level
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Being regular requires a calm mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland, a ness, not a mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Regularity is uniformity or smoothness without variation.

clue.text: Paid to be colonised

definitions.meaning: a bill that has been cleared
a land taken over and inhabited by newcomers

explanation.surface: Someone was paid to be colonised.
explanation.definitionFit: An account that is cleared has been discharged, and a territory people moved into and occupied has been populated.

clue.text: Suitable 'position on 'a quiet river

indicators.note: on means the position comes after the earlier parts

parts.note: p is piano, quiet in music
the Po is the main river of Italy
a site is a position

explanation.surface: A good spot beside a calm river.
explanation.walkthrough: In music p (piano) means quiet; the Po is Italy's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apposite is apt and relevant.

clue.text: The sort of revenue to be found in farming

parts.note: the land means farming, as in working on the land

explanation.surface: Tax income is found in agriculture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the British tax authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's tax collectors were called the Inland Revenue, so this word names that kind.

clue.text: See you, say, in the police station?

definitions.meaning: spoken, see you sounds like C U, the chemical symbol of this metal
a policeman, found at the station

explanation.surface: A goodbye said in the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: Cu is the chemical symbol for the metal, which said out loud sounds like see you.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal with symbol Cu, and British slang for a police officer.

clue.text: Cabinet-maker's offering of comfort 'to the' board

parts.note: to comfort is to console
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A furniture maker gives comfort to the directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a company board but is a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow table fixed against a wall on brackets, the kind of piece a furniture maker produces.

clue.text: Animal raised for a bit of wool

indicators.note: raised means read upwards, which in a down clue turns the word round

parts.note: a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature bred for its fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LION upwards in this down clue, giving NOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Noil is the short fibre combed out of wool before spinning.

clue.text: Rock in South' Africa

parts.note: a ridge of rock, and the gold-bearing seam of the Witwatersrand known by that name

explanation.surface: A geological feature in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The Witwatersrand gold field near Johannesburg is known as the Reef.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of rock near the sea surface, also a gold-bearing seam in mining.

clue.text: Sign deposition

explanation.surface: Put your name to a legal statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof shows itself as an indication, and a witness's sworn statement is testimony.

clue.text: Cunning ocean monster's habitat?

parts.note: the deep is the ocean
Loch Ness in Scotland is home to the legendary monster

explanation.surface: A crafty sea creature's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Deep can mean cunning, as in a deep one; the Loch Ness monster lives in Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deep is being crafty and hard to fathom, so profundity serves as cleverness.
